The impugned order dated 05.12.2022 is reproduced as under :-
"....
An application u/s 227 CrPC was moved on the LDOH seeking discharge of accused Pushpa and Govindi.
Arguments heard.

During the course of arguments, counsel for the accused argued that the allegations are omnibus in nature against the above said accused persons whereas in the matter under Section 498A IPC specific allegations have to be present to frame charges against them which is missing in the present matter as there are only bald statement of the complainant against both of them whereas Ld. APP opposed the same and argued that there are allegations of inflicting torture against mother in law Govindi Pant and Sister in law Pushpa for instigating her husband for torturing her and not allowing the complainant in matrimonial home.

Further there are allegations against both of them for demanding dowry and misbehaviour with the complainant by taunting Crl Rev No. 124/2023 Govindi Pant & Anr. Vs. State of NCT of Delhi & Anr.
Page No. 2 of 9 her for bringing more and more dowry . Therefore, in the light of specific allegations against them of misappropriation of dowry articles and infliction of cruelty upon complainant by them, the present application stands dismissed."

sentences.text: I have heard arguments of both the sides and perused the record of revision petition as well as record of trial court.

8. With respect to the power and scope of revision U/s 397 Cr.P.C., the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Amit Kapoor Vs. Ramesh Chander, (2012) 9 SCC 460 held as under :-
"The revisional jurisdiction of the Court u/s 397 CrPC can be exercised so as to examine the correctness, legality or propriety of an order passed by the trial court or the inferior court, as the case may be.

entities.text: Amit Kapoor Vs. Ramesh Chander, (2012) 9 SCC 460
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though Section 397 CrPC does not specifically use the expression "prevent abuse of process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice", the jurisdiction u/s 397 CrPC is a very limited one.

The legality,
propriety or correctness of an order passed by a court is the Crl Rev No. 124/2023 Govindi Pant & Anr. Vs. State of NCT of Delhi & Anr. Page No. 5 of 9 very foundation of exercise of jurisdiction u/s 397 CrPC but ultimately it also requires justice to be done.

entities.text: Crl Rev No. 124/2023 Govindi Pant & Anr. Vs. State of NCT of Delhi & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The jurisdiction can be exercised where there is palpable error,
non-compliance with the provisions of law, the decision is completely erroneous or where the judicial discretion is exercised arbitrarily."
9.
Vide the impugned order dated 05.12.2022, the Ld. Trial Court dealt with application U/s 227 Cr.P.C. moved by the revisionists i.e. accused no. 2 and 3 and dismissed the same.

At the outset, it may be noted that the correct provision of law as applicable is Section 239/240 Cr.P.C. since the FIR in question is a subject matter of trial of warrant case by a Magistrate(case instituted upon a police report).

Therefore, it would be apt to reproduce the correct provisions of law as under :-
"239.

When accused shall be discharged - If, upon considering the police report and the documents sent with it under section 173 and making such examination, if any, of the accused as the Magistrate thinks necessary and after giving the prosecution and the accused an opportunity of being heard, the Magistrate considers the charge against the accused to be groundless, he shall discharge the accused, and record his reasons for so doing.
240. Framing of Charge - (1) If, upon such consideration examination, if any, and hearing, the Magistrate is of opinion that there is ground for presuming that the accused has committed an offence triable under this Chapter, which such Magistrate is competent to try and which, in his opinion could be adequately punished by him,
he shall frame in writing a charge against the accused."
10. In Onkar Nath Mishra & Ors vs State (NCT Of Delhi) & Anr., 2008 (2) SCC 561, the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed as under :-
"11.

It is trite that at the stage of framing of charge the court is Crl Rev No. 124/2023 Govindi Pant &

sentences.text: What needs to be considered is whether there is a ground for presuming that the offence has been committed and not a ground for convicting the accused has been made out.

At that stage, even strong suspicion founded on material which leads the court to form a presumptive opinion as to the existence of the factual ingredients constituting the offence alleged would justify the framing of charge against the accused in respect of the commission of that offence."
11.

In the present case, the Ld. Trial Court in the impugned order dated 05.12.2022 observed that there are allegations against both the revisionists for demanding dowry and misbehaviour with the complainant and misappropriation of dowry articles.
Reading of the charge-sheet as filed in this case displayed that there are specific allegations made by the complainant against the revisionists who are her mother-in-law and sister-in-law.

There are specific allegations by the complainant in the charge-sheet that after the cancellation of the marriage of her husband's sister, he told about the marriage between him and the complainant to his family members and upon hearing this, her mother-in- law i.e. revisionist no. 1 told her not to disclose about the marriage to any other relative and asked her to arrange a flat for them and when she tried to tell that she is not in a position to arrange any money, her mother-in- law i.e. revisionist no. 1 told her to arrange the money from her mother and thereafter, she started instigating her son for the said demand.

It is further allegation in the complaint/ charge-sheet that the revisionists i.e. accused no. 2 and 3 did not allow the complainant to enter the house at Crl Rev No. 124/2023 Govindi Pant & Anr. Vs. State of NCT of Delhi & Anr. Page No. 7 of 9 Ranikhet, Almora, Uttrakhand and when she requested to stay with them, the mother-in-law i.e. revisionist no. 1 misbehaved with the complainant and taunting about her caste and sister-in-law i.e. accused no. 3/ revisionist no. 2 asked her to arrange a flat for them at Delhi and only then she would be allowed to enter the said house.

entities.text: Govindi Pant & Anr. Vs. State of NCT of Delhi & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are also allegations that upon refusal of their demands, the accused persons abused the complainant in most filthy language and complainant was thrown out of the house.
Ld. counsel for the revisionists argued that the allegations in the complaint/ charge-sheet are omnibus in nature and are false and frivolous.
He relied upon Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam & Ors. Vs. State of Bihar & Ors., 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 141.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam & Ors. Vs. State of Bihar & Ors., 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 141
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the allegations as noted above, are found to be specific and therefore, there is no force in the contention of the revisionists that the allegations leveled against them are general and omnibus in nature.
From the material as noted above, it cannot be said that the charge against the accused no. 2 and 3 is groundless and they deserve to be discharged.

Rather, from the allegations as made,
there is sufficient ground for presuming the commission of offence by the accused no. 2 and 3 i.e.
revisionists herein and consequently, makes out a case for framing of charge against them.
Thus, the impugned order dated 05.12.2022 passed by Ld. Trial Court suffers no error.
The authority relied upon by the Ld. counsel for revisionists is respectfully differentiated and is of no help to revisionists.

12. Thus, in view of the above discussion, I do not find any illegality or perversity in the impugned order dated 05.12.2022 passed by Crl Rev No. 124/2023 Govindi Pant & Anr. Vs. Metropolitan Magistrate-03 (Mahila Court), Central District, Delhi in dismissing the application U/s 227 Cr.P.C. moved on behalf of accused no. 2 and 3 namely Govindi Pant and Pushpa Pant seeking their discharge.
